tools.name: merges.list
tools.description:
List ready merges awaiting consent or held, with frozen effective targets and verification evidence.

Returns: JSON array ordered by slug: kind, target, branch, candidate, reason, verification and node completeness.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

tools.name: landings.list
tools.description:
Deprecated alias for merges.list. List ready merges awaiting consent or held, with frozen effective targets and verification evidence.

Returns: JSON array ordered by slug: kind, target, branch, candidate, reason, verification and node completeness.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

tools.name: tickets.tree
tools.description:
Read the exhaustive source ticket tree, including completed tickets and empty nodes.

Returns: {root, children, diagnostics}: source metadata ancestry, distinct from frozen build targets.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

tools.name: builds.list
tools.description:
List one repository’s builds, newest first, with effective status derived from the build log.

Returns: JSON array of build summaries: slug, ticket ref, effective status, phase/round/attempt, PR number/url/state, updatedAt, lease health, and durable-event progress.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

scope.description: Which builds to include: "active" (running, paused, or blocked — the default), "queued", or "all".

tools.name: builds.get
tools.description:
Show detailed state for one build: open escalations, verify progress, PR lifecycle, lease health, and the dashboard row.

Returns: {detail, dashboardRow}: the full build detail projection and the dashboard row a terminal dashboard would render (null when the build has no dashboard row).

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

slug.description: Build slug identifying one build in the store.

tools.name: builds.events
tools.description:
Read one build’s event log after a cursor, optionally waiting (bounded, ≤30s) for new events — the polling companion to builds.get.

Returns: {events, cursor}: the new events in sequence order (each with seq, ts, actor, type, payload) and the cursor to pass next time — the last returned event’s seq, or the requested cursor when the page is empty.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

slug.description: Build slug identifying one build in the store.

cursor.description: Event sequence cursor: return build events with seq strictly greater than this (0 = the whole log).

waitSeconds.description: Bounded wait: hold the call for at most this many seconds waiting for at least one new event before returning an empty page (0–30; 0 returns immediately).

tools.name: builds.artifact
tools.description:
Download one of a build’s deposited artifacts by kind and optional revision.

Returns: The artifact metadata {kind, revision, blobRef, createdAt} plus contentBase64: the exact artifact bytes base64-encoded. Decode contentBase64 to recover the download; the bytes are identical to the operator API’s artifact download body.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

slug.description: Build slug identifying one build in the store.

rev.description: Artifact revision to fetch; omit for the latest revision of the kind.

tools.name: builds.restack
tools.description:
Request a node restack onto its parent. Paused or blocked nodes retain demand until normal safety gates permit execution; refuses leaves, unopened and terminal nodes.

Returns: {slug, request, coalesced, waiting}: a durable request receipt; execution is asynchronous.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

slug.description: Build slug identifying one build in the store.

tools.name: builds.control
tools.description:
Pause immediately suspends a live agent session. Resume continues where stopped when supported; remote and unsupported sessions rerun fresh. Request a durable control for one active build: pause/cancel-pause, resume, hold or merge — or the destructive abort and discard. Merge requires a ready candidate; hold withdraws merge consent.

Returns: Either {kind: "command", slug, command, event} for an accepted control, or {kind: "answer-required", slug, escalationIds} when a resume needs its open escalations answered first.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

slug.description: Build slug identifying one build in the store.

action.description: Control to request: "pause" (or "cancel-pause" to revoke a pending pause), "resume" a paused build, "merge" (deprecated alias "land") for merge consent or "hold" to withdraw consent — or the destructive "abort" (cancels the build, cleans up its PR and workspace, returns the ticket to triage) and "discard" (dequeue a queued build).

tools.name: builds.answer
tools.description:
Answer a blocked build’s open escalations: guidance text, a bare retry, a dismissal of the cited findings, a review-round ceiling, or a spec revision (destructive — replaces the spec). Leaves require an escalation and restart from plan; idle collecting or verification-failed nodes may revise without an escalation and recollect for verification.

Returns: The controlBuild answer result: {kind: "answered", slug, count, resolution, resumed, …} describing how many escalations were answered and with what.

tools.name: repository.status
tools.description:
Report one repository’s durable dispatcher settings and journal state.

Returns: The repository status projection: ticket intake, repository-wide pause, claim-time auto-merge default, and the harvest/dispatch journal state the sessionless CLI and dashboard read.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

tools.name: repository.settings
tools.description:
Set or toggle a durable repository setting: ticket intake or the claim-time auto-merge default.

Returns: {enabled, event}: the resulting durable value and the appended repository event.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

setting.description: "intake" gates whether new tickets may be claimed.

enabled.description: Set the value explicitly; omit to toggle the current durable value.

tools.name: repository.bulk_control
tools.description:
Pause or resume the whole repository: hold queued builds, set intake, and request per-build pause/resume in one walk.

Returns: {direction, slugs, paused, intake}: the direction, the slugs that received a durable request, and the repository-wide hold/intake values written. A partial walk surfaces as a refusal with code "bulk-partial" and a progress object naming what merged.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

action.description: "pause" holds every queued build, turns intake off, and requests pause on every running build without a pending pause; "resume" reverses all three.

tools.name: harvest.status
tools.description:
Report one repository’s observation-harvest state: unresolved workflows, pending proposals, and their paper trail.

Returns: The harvest status projection the sessionless `ab harvest status` renders.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

tools.name: harvest.control
tools.description:
Toggle the repository’s harvest gate, or act on the concrete harvest run the dashboard captured.

Returns: For "toggle-gate": {command: "pause"|"resume", event}. For a run action: {action, event} — the action the dashboard offered for that run.

labels.description: Narrow the list to tickets carrying every named label.

tools.name: tickets.get

tools.description:
Read the repository’s operator-notes artifact — the shared notes an operator agent leaves for the next round.

Returns: {document, revision, metadata}: the latest revision’s UTF-8 text, its artifact revision, and its deposit metadata (writer identity). An empty document with null revision/metadata when no notes exist yet.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

tools.name: notes.write
tools.description:
Deposit a new revision of the repository’s operator-notes artifact, attributed to the caller.

Returns: {revision, blobRef, createdAt}: the newly deposited revision. The kind is retention-managed: only the newest 200 revisions (the store’s configured maxRevisions) survive.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

document.description: The complete replacement notes document (UTF-8 text); an empty string clears the notes.

tools.name: sandbox.exec
tools.description:
Run one shell command inside your operator sandbox: a persistent, credential-free environment provisioned from the repository (first call provisions; later calls reuse it). The command waits at most 300 seconds; on expiry it is killed and the tool fails with code "sandbox-exec-timeout". Stdout and stderr are each truncated at 65,536 bytes with a "[truncated by autobuild: output exceeded 65536 bytes]" marker. The environment holds no store, forge, or model credentials — the typed tools remain the only route to build state.

Returns: {exitCode, stdout, stderr}: the command’s exit status and truncated output streams.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

command.description: Shell command to run inside the operator sandbox.

cwd.description: Working directory for the command, relative to the checkout; defaults to the checkout root. Absolute paths and ".." escapes are refused.

timeoutSeconds.description: Bounded wait for the command, 1-300 seconds (default 120). On expiry the command is killed and the tool fails with code "sandbox-exec-timeout".

tools.name: sandbox.start
tools.description:
Launch one shell command detached inside your operator sandbox and return immediately. Pair with sandbox.wait to observe it. Calls against one environment are serialized; a detached command is tracked only by the serving process.

Returns: {commandId}: the id to pass to sandbox.wait.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

command.description: Shell command to launch detached inside the operator sandbox.

cwd.description: Working directory for the command, relative to the checkout; defaults to the checkout root. Absolute paths and ".." escapes are refused.

tools.name: sandbox.wait
tools.description:
Wait, bounded (0–300 seconds), on a command started with sandbox.start. Returns state "running" (poll again) or "exited" with the exit code and output so far. Remote providers report command output only after exit, so a running command shows no output there.

Returns: {state, exitCode?, stdout?, stderr?}: the command state; once exited, its exit code and truncated output streams; while running, the streamed output so far when the provider reports it (Vercel reports output only after exit).

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

commandId.description: Command id returned by a previous sandbox.start.

waitSeconds.description: Bounded wait, 0-300 seconds. Returns state "running" (no output on remote providers, which report output only after exit) or "exited" with the exit code and output so far.

tools.name: sandbox.read_file
tools.description:
Read one file from your operator sandbox, rooted at the checkout. Absolute paths and ".." escapes are refused.

Returns: {encoding, content}: the file bytes — "utf8" when they decode as UTF-8, else "base64".

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

path.description: File path relative to the checkout. Absolute paths and ".." escapes are refused.

tools.name: sandbox.write_file
tools.description:
Write one file inside your operator sandbox, rooted at the checkout (parent directories are created). Absolute paths and ".." escapes are refused; content is bounded at 1 MiB after decoding.

Returns: {path}: the written path, confirming the durable write.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

path.description: File path relative to the checkout. Absolute paths and ".." escapes are refused.

content.description: File content (see encoding); at most 1 MiB after decoding.

tools.name: sandbox.reset
tools.description:
Destructively reset your operator sandbox: discard every change, purge the environment and its snapshots, and re-provision fresh from the current base branch head. Use when the environment is wedged or its checkout is dirty beyond repair.

Returns: {ok: true}: the environment was released and re-provisioned from the current base head.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

tools.name: sandbox.publish
tools.description:
Publish your operator sandbox's work as a pull request: push the checkout's current head commit (or an explicit commit) to your operator's dedicated branch and open or update a PR against the base branch. Refuses when the checkout has uncommitted changes (tracked or untracked; the sandbox's own provisioning marker is excluded), when the commit is not a descendant of the base head recorded at provision or reset time, or when the base branch head itself would be published. The sandbox itself never pushes and holds no credential — the push and PR creation are kernel plumbing; a publication is a durable repository-journal fact. PR only: the base branch is never pushed to.

Returns: {branch, sha, pr: {number, url, headSha}}: the publication branch, the published commit, and the opened or updated pull request.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

body.description: Optional pull-request body, at most 65,536 characters; an attribution block naming the operator and session is appended automatically.

commit.description: Optional commit-ish to publish instead of the checkout HEAD; must resolve to a commit that is a descendant of the base head recorded at provision or reset time.

result.instructions: Autobuild operator tools for the repositories this deployment serves: builds, repository and harvest controls, tickets, and operator notes. Autobuild runs builds from tickets: a dispatcher claims groomed tickets, an embedded agent implements each build through plan/implement/verify rounds, and every durable action is attributed. Call `repositories.list` first to discover which repository identities this deployment serves; every tool names its repository explicitly via `repo`. Mutating tools append durable, human-attributed events under the signed-in operator who authorized this client; destructive controls are annotated. Read tools mirror the operator API routes — every result equals the corresponding route — and `builds.events` after a cursor is the polling companion to `builds.get`.

tools.name: builds.control
tools.description:
Pause immediately suspends a live agent session. Resume continues where stopped when supported; remote and unsupported sessions rerun fresh. Request a durable control for one active build: pause/cancel-pause, resume, hold or merge — or the destructive abort and discard. Merge requires a ready candidate; hold withdraws merge consent.

Returns: Either {kind: "command", slug, command, event} for an accepted control, or {kind: "answer-required", slug, escalationIds} when a resume needs its open escalations answered first.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

slug.description: Build slug identifying one build in the store.

action.description: Control to request: "pause" (or "cancel-pause" to revoke a pending pause), "resume" a paused build, "merge" (deprecated alias "land") for merge consent or "hold" to withdraw consent — or the destructive "abort" (cancels the build, cleans up its PR and workspace, returns the ticket to triage) and "discard" (dequeue a queued build).

tools.name: builds.answer
tools.description:
Answer a blocked build’s open escalations: guidance text, a bare retry, a dismissal of the cited findings, a review-round ceiling, or a spec revision (destructive — replaces the spec). Leaves require an escalation and restart from plan; idle collecting or verification-failed nodes may revise without an escalation and recollect for verification.

Returns: The controlBuild answer result: {kind: "answered", slug, count, resolution, resumed, …} describing how many escalations were answered and with what.

tools.name: sandbox.exec
tools.description:
Run one shell command inside your operator sandbox: a persistent, credential-free environment provisioned from the repository (first call provisions; later calls reuse it). The command waits at most 300 seconds; on expiry it is killed and the tool fails with code "sandbox-exec-timeout". Stdout and stderr are each truncated at 65,536 bytes with a "[truncated by autobuild: output exceeded 65536 bytes]" marker. The environment holds no store, forge, or model credentials — the typed tools remain the only route to build state.

Returns: {exitCode, stdout, stderr}: the command’s exit status and truncated output streams.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

command.description: Shell command to run inside the operator sandbox.

cwd.description: Working directory for the command, relative to the checkout; defaults to the checkout root. Absolute paths and ".." escapes are refused.

timeoutSeconds.description: Bounded wait for the command, 1-300 seconds (default 120). On expiry the command is killed and the tool fails with code "sandbox-exec-timeout".

tools.name: sandbox.start
tools.description:
Launch one shell command detached inside your operator sandbox and return immediately. Pair with sandbox.wait to observe it. Calls against one environment are serialized; a detached command is tracked only by the serving process.

Returns: {commandId}: the id to pass to sandbox.wait.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

command.description: Shell command to launch detached inside the operator sandbox.

cwd.description: Working directory for the command, relative to the checkout; defaults to the checkout root. Absolute paths and ".." escapes are refused.

tools.name: sandbox.wait
tools.description:
Wait, bounded (0–300 seconds), on a command started with sandbox.start. Returns state "running" (poll again) or "exited" with the exit code and output so far. Remote providers report command output only after exit, so a running command shows no output there.

Returns: {state, exitCode?, stdout?, stderr?}: the command state; once exited, its exit code and truncated output streams; while running, the streamed output so far when the provider reports it (Vercel reports output only after exit).

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

commandId.description: Command id returned by a previous sandbox.start.

waitSeconds.description: Bounded wait, 0-300 seconds. Returns state "running" (no output on remote providers, which report output only after exit) or "exited" with the exit code and output so far.

tools.name: sandbox.read_file

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

path.description: File path relative to the checkout. Absolute paths and ".." escapes are refused.

tools.name: sandbox.write_file
tools.description:
Write one file inside your operator sandbox, rooted at the checkout (parent directories are created). Absolute paths and ".." escapes are refused; content is bounded at 1 MiB after decoding.

Returns: {path}: the written path, confirming the durable write.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

path.description: File path relative to the checkout. Absolute paths and ".." escapes are refused.

content.description: File content (see encoding); at most 1 MiB after decoding.

tools.name: sandbox.reset
tools.description:
Destructively reset your operator sandbox: discard every change, purge the environment and its snapshots, and re-provision fresh from the current base branch head. Use when the environment is wedged or its checkout is dirty beyond repair.

Returns: {ok: true}: the environment was released and re-provisioned from the current base head.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

tools.name: sandbox.publish
tools.description:
Publish your operator sandbox's work as a pull request: push the checkout's current head commit (or an explicit commit) to your operator's dedicated branch and open or update a PR against the base branch. Refuses when the checkout has uncommitted changes (tracked or untracked; the sandbox's own provisioning marker is excluded), when the commit is not a descendant of the base head recorded at provision or reset time, or when the base branch head itself would be published. The sandbox itself never pushes and holds no credential — the push and PR creation are kernel plumbing; a publication is a durable repository-journal fact. PR only: the base branch is never pushed to.

Returns: {branch, sha, pr: {number, url, headSha}}: the publication branch, the published commit, and the opened or updated pull request.

repo.description: Repository identity as the store keys it: the checkout’s normalized origin URL (e.g. "https://github.com/acme/widgets").

body.description: Optional pull-request body, at most 65,536 characters; an attribution block naming the operator and session is appended automatically.

commit.description: Optional commit-ish to publish instead of the checkout HEAD; must resolve to a commit that is a descendant of the base head recorded at provision or reset time.
